megarac@megarac-desktop:~$ ipmitool -I lanplus -H 172.16.97.21 -U root -P 0penBmc -C 17 raw 0x04 0x02 0x04 0x01 0x01 0x01 0x59 0x01 0x00

Hello, thank you for testing.

On one of our downstream platforms, I can reproduce the issue with the `ipmitool event` command:

```
$ ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc_ip> -U root -P 0penBmc event <sensor> ucr
Finding sensor <sensor>... ok
0 | Pre-Init |0000000000| <sensor id> | Upper Critical going high | Asserted
Platform Event Message command failed: Request data length invalid
```

I also tested on Romulus and observed the same completion code behavior as you did. In my Romulus setup, both the original code and the patched code return 0xFF due to the SEL backend path, so the exact completion code appears to be platform dependent.

The main issue I am trying to address is the payload parsing offset.

For a LAN/RMCP+ Platform Event Message, the request arrives on channel 1 with the following payload:

```
04 01 01 01 59 01 00
```

According to IPMI v2.0 (Table 29), this should be interpreted as:
```
EvMRev         = 0x04
Sensor Type    = 0x01
Sensor Number  = 0x01
Event Dir/Type = 0x01
Event Data 1   = 0x59
Event Data 2   = 0x01
Event Data 3   = 0x00
```

However, the original implementation always treats the request as a System Interface Platform Event Message and unconditionally skips the first byte (`raw + 1`).

As a result, the payload is parsed with a one-byte offset.

[Original code]
```none
eventRevision=1
sensorType=1
sensorNumber=1
eventDirectionType=89
data0=1
```

[Patched code]
```none
eventRevision=4
sensorType=1
sensorNumber=1
eventDirectionType=1
data0=89
```

This matches the expected field layout defined by IPMI v2.0 Table 29.

For reference, I temporarily added the following debug logs to verify the payload and parsing behavior:

```diff
diff --git a/sensorhandler.cpp b/sensorhandler.cpp
index 9ab3612..3221f8a 100644
--- a/sensorhandler.cpp
+++ b/sensorhandler.cpp
@@ -1530,6 +1530,15 @@ static bool isFromSystemChannel()
 ipmi::RspType<> ipmicmdPlatformEvent(ipmi::Context::ptr& ctx,
                                      const std::vector<uint8_t>& data)
 {
+    lg2::info("PlatformEvent: channel={CHANNEL}, size={SIZE}",
+          "CHANNEL", ctx->channel, "SIZE", data.size());
+
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < data.size(); ++i)
+    {
+        lg2::info("PlatformEvent: data[{INDEX}]={BYTE}",
+                  "INDEX", i, "BYTE", data[i]);
+    }
+
     size_t paraLen = data.size();
     if (paraLen < selSystemEventSizeWith1Bytes ||
         paraLen > selSystemEventSizeWith3Bytes)
@@ -1558,6 +1567,14 @@ ipmi::RspType<> ipmicmdPlatformEvent(ipmi::Context::ptr& ctx,
         // TODO GenratorID for IPMB is combination of RqSA and RqLUN
     }
 
+    lg2::info("PlatformEvent: eventRevision={REV}, sensorType={TYPE}, "
+          "sensorNumber={NUM}, eventDirectionType={EVENT}, data0={DATA0}",
+          "REV", req->eventMessageRevision,
+          "TYPE", req->sensorType,
+          "NUM", req->sensorNumber,
+          "EVENT", req->eventDirectionType,
+          "DATA0", req->data[0]);
+
     // Content of event data field depends on sensor class.
     // When data0 bit[5:4] is non-zero, valid data counts is 3.
     // When data0 bit[7:6] is non-zero, valid data counts is 2.
```

Parsing was previously offset by one byte for LAN channel requests because the handler always assumed System Interface format and skipped byte 0; the patch makes channel-aware decoding, so payload fields now match IPMI Table 29 expectations.
